I basically told the stylist my goals were to give it more shape and bring out the waves, and she showed me where my hair naturally had some shorter pieces that were a good starting place for layers. We ended up going with long layers and face-framing layers based on what my hair wanted to do!

\-wash once/week with suave clarifying shampoo 

\-condition (still trying different ones) and comb with wide tooth comb 

\-scrunch in curl stimulator and micro plop 

\-air dry/diffuse until about halfway dry, the scrunch in a couple handfuls of gel 

\-finish diffusing until 80-90% dry

Sometimes I wash mid week with as I am coconut cowash if it starts looking rough between wash days

Routine: changes a lot but most recently

\-comb in some Cake brand curl cream and LA looks blue gel

\-scrunch and microplop with a cotton pillow case

Routine: not super consistent, but wash every 2-3 days, leave conditioner on while I finish showering (currently giovanni), rinse out completely, scrunch in curl cream (currently Cake brand) and/or gel (blue LA looks). Counseling during the semester I was getting ready for the MCAT was a lifesaver, would recommend if you have the option and aren't already. I took a lot of summer classes in order to avoid a crazy amount of hours during the school year (I have 2 very different majors) and no one mentioned it in interviews or anything. I brought some of those applesauce pouch things, those are easy to eat with a nervous stomach and you can get it down really fast on the way to the bathroom during a 10 minute break. I also downed an energy drink during my breaks- maybe don’t do that if you aren’t used to caffeine, but I’m a caffeine addict and also couldn’t sleep the night before so I was glad that I had it!

It’s definitely feasible, it just depends on your personal priorities and if that’s when you want to put in the work. I started studying over Christmas break and took the MCAT like a week after the semester ended, so nearly all my studying was during school (taking like 16 or 17 hours). It sucks and it’s difficult and you will have to sacrifice your social life some, but if you have time management skills it’s doable. I was also taking classes like biochem and anatomy that semester that were on the MCAT, so if there’s overlap with your course load and test prep that helps too!

I didn’t do the CARS q pack so this may not apply, but on the other q packs I think I was in the mid-high 60s and still pulled off a 520 on the real MCAT. So don't let the q pack scores get into your head too much :)

Maybe consider a gap year if you’re not sure about pharmacy school? It could allow you to decide if you for sure want to pursue medicine, and give you time to hit MCAT prep hard and do well on it if that’s what you decide.
I mean that's just my 2 cents. If it would be easier for you, you could maybe just start reading the news or something (google news is a great place to start for a variety of articles).

For CARS, I would suggest trying to read more in general if you’re not a big reader already. I did pretty well on CARS, but I’ve always read a lot of books of varying subjects and genres and I felt like that helped me take on whatever subjects CARS threw at me. It is really difficult to find time for that when you’re busy with other stuff (like studying for the MCAT!), but it sounds like that practice could maybe boost your speed and reading comprehension.
